What a /22 means

A /22 gives 1,022 usable hosts, a good fit for a department, a floor or a medium branch office.

The prefix length is the number of leading bits that identify the network. A /22 uses 22 network bits and leaves 10 host bits, so the block contains 1,024 addresses. Usable hosts: 2(32−22) − 2 = 1,024 − 2 = 1,022.

Configuration examples

Cisco IOS

interface Vlan10
 ip address 172.16.0.1 255.255.252.0
!
access-list 10 permit 172.16.0.0 0.0.3.255

Juniper Junos

set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 172.16.0.1/22

Linux

ip addr add 172.16.0.1/22 dev eth0

Addresses shown are examples from private or documentation space. Replace them with your own plan.

FAQ

How many usable hosts are in a /22?

1,022. A /22 has 1,024 addresses; the first is the network address and the last is the broadcast address, so 1,022 are usable.

What is the subnet mask for /22?

255.255.252.0. The wildcard mask, used in ACLs and OSPF network statements, is 0.0.3.255.
